summary: 11 concrete, comment-endorsed tools, services, and publications selected from a verified 30-story HN front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: NERV Disaster Prevention app
items.summary: A Japanese disaster-alert app with real-time earthquake and seismic-intensity updates.
items.why_included: A firsthand user called it faster than official sources and useful enough to visualize an arriving shockwave.
items.evidence: A commenter said the NERV app delivers real-time alerts faster than official sources and described watching an earthquake's shockwave before feeling it.

evidence_sources.author: timr
evidence_sources.excerpt: The Nerv app is quite good. It usually gives real-time alerts faster than the official sources.

items.name: Micropia
items.summary: An Amsterdam museum dedicated to microbes and their role in everyday life.
items.why_included: It was directly recommended as a memorable in-person science experience.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended Micropia, highlighting its displays of foods and drinks aging over days to years.

evidence_sources.author: carschno
evidence_sources.excerpt: if you are ever in Amsterdam, I recommend to visit the Micropia museum

items.name: OpenSpec
items.summary: A structured specification workflow for keeping coding-agent plans parseable and actionable.
items.why_included: It was recommended as an existing implementation of a proposed plan-scaffolding and validation workflow.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended OpenSpec as a tool implementing reusable plan templates, validation, and workflow-state evaluation.

evidence_sources.author: LiveTheDream
evidence_sources.excerpt: You should take a look at OpenSpec[0]. It implements your points 1-3.

items.name: Agent Scaffold
items.summary: A CLI for structured agent plans, workflow transitions, and plan-file validation.
items.why_included: Its creator reported that dogfooding it reduced long-run agent drift, while clearly flagging that the codebase remains unfinished.
items.evidence: The creator said the tool scaffolds and validates structured plans, and that their own use suggested it let Claude run longer with less drift.

evidence_sources.author: nicoty
evidence_sources.excerpt: So far, I've been dogfooding the tool and it seems promising: I can leave Claude running for longer and it doesn't drift as much.

items.name: Delayed Gratification
items.source_story_title: Delayed Gratification – Proud to Be 'Last to Breaking News'
items.summary: A print-led slow-journalism magazine that revisits news after the immediate cycle.
items.why_included: A former subscriber strongly endorsed its design, writing, and physical production despite deciding it was not their personal reading habit.
items.evidence: A former subscriber called the publication beautifully designed and well written, and said it was worth trying for readers drawn to the premise.

evidence_sources.author: petercooper
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's beautifully designed, well written, good paper stock, the works. If the idea appeals to you, it's worth trying.

items.name: Tangle News
items.source_story_title: Delayed Gratification – Proud to Be 'Last to Breaking News'
items.summary: A weekday news digest that gives detailed breakdowns of four major stories each week.
items.why_included: It was positively recommended as a practical middle ground between breaking-news churn and long-delay retrospectives.
items.evidence: A commenter said Tangle News strikes a good balance, with detailed coverage of four top stories each week.

evidence_sources.author: Brendinooo
evidence_sources.excerpt: Tangle News[0] strikes a pretty good balance here.

items.name: Verity
items.source_story_title: Delayed Gratification – Proud to Be 'Last to Breaking News'
items.summary: A news service that presents competing framing and sourcing around current stories.
items.why_included: It was suggested as a concrete option for readers seeking to compare competing narratives.
items.evidence: A commenter suggested Verity for readers interested in seeing both sides of news spin.

evidence_sources.author: cachvico
evidence_sources.excerpt: https://www.verity.news/ might be interesting for you; they try to show you both sides of the spin.

items.name: Pi Agent
items.source_story_title: Using an open model feels surprisingly good
items.summary: A lightweight coding-agent harness focused on a lean, manual workflow.
items.why_included: It was explicitly recommended as an even leaner alternative in a discussion about open-model coding setups.
items.evidence: A commenter described Pi Agent as leaner-feeling and said it was worth trying.

evidence_sources.author: roywiggins
evidence_sources.excerpt: Pi Agent is even leaner feeling, it's worth a try.

items.name: Yap
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Yap – OSS on-device voice dictation for macOS with no model to download
items.summary: An open-source macOS dictation app built on on-device speech APIs.
items.why_included: A commenter building a personal knowledge tool saw it as a promising way to add direct voice interaction.
items.evidence: A commenter called Yap a great opportunity for adding voice interaction to their project.

evidence_sources.author: 9dev
evidence_sources.excerpt: Yap looks like a great opportunity to learn!

items.name: KineStop
items.summary: An Android motion-cue app designed to reduce screen-induced travel sickness.
items.why_included: A firsthand user said it worked better for them than Apple's equivalent, while noting its permissions trade-off.
items.evidence: A commenter said KineStop worked better for them than Apple's iOS implementation, but noted that it needs invasive permissions.

evidence_sources.author: Cider9986
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use KineStop and it works better than Apple's version on iOS did for me.

items.name: security-skills
items.summary: A collection of pentesting skills distilled from public HackerOne disclosures.
items.why_included: It was directly recommended to pentesters as a reusable, concrete knowledge pack.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended the skills collection to pentesters and described it as distilled from 4,000 public HackerOne disclosures.

evidence_sources.author: mkagenius
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you are a pentester who uses mitmproxy you can check out security skills distilled from 4000 Hackerone public disclosures
